name: Cook Islands
summary: A British blue ensign with a ring of fifteen white stars in the fly. The Cook Islands are self-governing in free association with New Zealand.
origin: The Cook Islands became self-governing in 1965. A green flag with a circle of yellow stars was used from 1973 to 1979. The current blue ensign was adopted on 4 August 1979.

colors.name: Blue
colors.meaning: The Pacific Ocean and the peaceful nature of the people.

symbols.name: Fifteen stars
symbols.meaning: The fifteen islands; the circle represents unity.

symbols.name: Union Flag
symbols.meaning: Historical links with Britain and New Zealand.

facts: Cook Islanders are New Zealand citizens.
The previous green flag of 1973–1979 is still sometimes flown as a cultural symbol.
The islands are named after Captain James Cook.
clues: A blue ensign with a circle of fifteen white stars.
Its stars stand for fifteen islands.
Its islands are in free association with a Pacific neighbour.
